purpose: Explain when geostatistical, machine-learning and residual-fusion strategies succeed or fail under spatial extrapolation.

geometry.primary: Use de-identified Qidashan assay coordinates and frozen five-block assignments.

scenarios.mechanism: Stationary anisotropic Gaussian random field with correctly specified trend and covariance.
Strong directional anisotropy while prediction assumes the frozen isotropic/z-scaled distance.
Contiguous geological domains with abrupt mean shifts and no domain indicator.
A fault plane offsets the latent field and changes local continuity.
Latent point support is averaged over variable interval lengths while models use midpoint features.
Continuity range is shorter than the distance from the held-out sector to training support.
A target-derived neighbourhood feature is added as an explicitly nondeployable positive control.

methods.M1_idw: Frozen local IDW: k=8, power=2, z_scale=0.25.
methods.M2_ordinary_kriging: Local ordinary kriging with exponential variogram fitted on outer-training targets; k=24, z_scale=0.25.
methods.M3_catboost_coordinates: Fixed CatBoost on coordinate and trajectory/support features.
methods.M4_crossfitted_residual_kriging: Fixed CatBoost trend plus residual kriging from spatially cross-fitted outer-training residuals.

validation.outer_scheme: the frozen five contiguous spatial blocks
validation.inner_residual_scheme: three-fold spatial-group cross-fitting inside each outer-training set
boundary_metrics: probability Delta R2 positive across replicates

hypotheses.H1: Ordinary and residual kriging help in S0 when covariance is transferable.
hypotheses.H2: Residual fusion loses benefit or becomes harmful under S1-S5.
hypotheses.H3: Random or target-leaking validation produces inflated accuracy in S6.
hypotheses.H4: No single method dominates all mechanisms.

selection_policy: No scenario, replicate, method or result may be removed because of unfavourable performance.
